body: Great beach clean gently sloping beach into sea great shore breaks for body surfing We ate lunch and supper atBest Beach Bar Restaurant delicious fresh foodAdults and kids really having fun great atmosphere

body: Beautiful, flat sloping beach to the sea, which seems very clean and tidy. In/at the small restaurants on the beach there is a very relaxed atmosphere. Nobody became intrusive, everything “lazy”, just beautiful, just like before. body: We stayed at Plam Paradise Vilas on this beach. The beach is beautiful, but we were there in early October when the seas are still a bit rough. Being from Australia and living near the beach we were able to swim, but the the waves were a strong shore dumps and behind the waves curents were very strong. So just be careful at this time of year when swimming. We would have loved to see the beach when it was calmer. A really pretty place.
title: A bit rough was ok for experienced swimmers

body: It was a bit tricky swimming in the beaches in the main stretch in Tangalle, so my brother and I decideed to try out Goyambokka.The beach is a kind of tucked away cove surrounded by coconut trees and with a few restaurants behind the sand. The beach is very small, but as it was low season there were very few tourists so it felt very secluded and tranquil. The swimming was much better than in Tangalle, as although there are some strong waves they are not quite as strong as on the main stretch of Tangalle and water is fairly shallow. That being said, we still weren’t able to properly swim, more just wade in and jump about a bit, as the water is too shallow for proper swimming and if you go too far out you go beyond the surf where it is probably a bit dangerous. Also be aware there is still a rip tide of sorts, so keep a close eye on children if you have them.The restaurants did not seem to have elecricity as all the food and drink was stores in coolers, also meaning the range of options were limited. However, you can get noodles, rice, various more Wearern dishes if you want. We got a spiced grilled fish with chips which was delicious.*How to get there*Most of the tourists there seemed to be staying in one of the Cabanas next to the beach, however we were coming in from Tangalle town.We took a bus from the terrapin pond which is close to the base hospital and girls school. Not sure which bus, we just stood on the side of the pond (photo attached) and asked for Goyambokka and eventually a bus driver let us on, cost 20 rupees each. Just beware the buses were very busy and because it is a short distance, about 4 to 5 minutes, a fair few buses would not let us on. We then asked the conductor to let us know when we were at Goyambokka and he told us when. We also walked once, just along the road and that took us about 45 mins, but it is not ideal. A tuk tuk on another occasion cost us 250 rupees which is likely an extortionate tourist price but there you go.I’d recommend this beach for a more secluded experience and if you are happy to just sunbathe and have the occasional dip in the water, as there is nothing else there.
title: Lovely beach, secluded, swimming okay

body: After spending a few days on the crowded beach in Mirissa, we were delighted to find Goyambokka Beach. It had the right level of activity for us - a few restaurants, people around, but very tranquil. There were also lots of sun loungers free, which we didn't have to pay to use. body: It's a busy place by standards of the region. But if you don't mind a bit of the crowd, then it's a great place to get a chair and enjoy the beautiful beach.Chairs seem to cost 1000 Rupees for two. Or you can eat a seafood lunch and your chair is free. The seafood lunch seemed to be dramatically overpriced to offset it though. We chose to just pay for the chair, which seemed fair.

body: This was my favourite out of several beautiful beaches along the coast between Tangalle and Galle. Mainly because it was not crowded. There are a few places to eat and the food was basic but good.The one I ate at gave you the sunbed all day for free if you agreed to eat there at lunch.People have commented that it's expensive. Well you'll find that after travelling the non-beach areas of Sri Lanka, suddenly EVERYTHING in this stretch is double or triple the price you've been paying e.g curry and rice I'd usually had for 300 now cost 1000.

body: We spent a few weeks travelling around Sri Lanka and this was one of our favourite beaches, It's not a massive beach but has a chilled vibe and isn't as busy as many of the other beaches we visited. There are a few nice seafood restaurants along the beach not cheap but pretty standard prices.If your looking for somewhere to switch off and get away for a while I would highly recommend this place.

As they are right on the beach and in the elements some of the beds etc were needing to be disposed of or repaired but guess they are waiting until the new season.For a quieter and just as nice beach 1km further out of Tangalle is Amanwella which we preferred (but nowhere for food so take water!)
title: Nice beach but a bit run down

body: The water is great for body surfing. You can lay out on the many shaded lounge chairs with a fresh young coconut from any of the restaurant shacks along the beach. There were a few amount of people, but definitely way less crowded, and smaller than Mirissa Beach.
title: Beautiful sand and waters

body: There is no doubt that this beach is picture perfect to look at. Small, sandy cove fringed with palm trees. However, we stayed here for 2 weeks and on only one day was the surf reasonable. All other days there were huge dumping waves with a very strong undertow. This churned up the sand so the water was not pleasant. We found the food at the beach huts to be mediocre at best and certainly not value for money.
title: Beautiful beach but....

body: It's a beautiful beach - small and relatively quiet. Surprisingly good food in the beach shacks. But careful of the waves. You can have fun but we had to be in the water with our 8 & 11 year olds to keep an eye on them. Swimming is impossible unless you are a strong swimmer.
title: Beautiful beach - a little rough

body: Stayed at the Whispering House with our family with a short walk to the beautiful beach. There can be some pretty powerful waves with a very strong undertow — perfect for our 12yo and his dad. Our 10yo daughter would join in occasionally and our 6yo was perfectly happy to play in the sand and lighter surf. Her younger cousins were there (2 & 3yo), and they stayed in their life jackets enjoying the surf and sand. If you eat/order drinks at one of the beach shacks, you get a lounge with shade at no cost. Our usual spot was at the Krishan fish place. Best French fries ever and excellent food all the way round. Very fresh.
title: Stunning beach with some excellent food

body: Gyombokka is a lovely horseshoe beach of the tropical paradise ilk. It remains fairly low key with 3 or 4 beach hut restaurants that fringe the sands and you can grab some lunch or a beer. The sea can get rough but is definitely swimmable if you know what you are doing. The hut owners charge you Rs 500 to rent a beach bed which is mildly annoying. Otherwise a great spot with a nice vibe.
title: Slice of paradise

body: Rustic and less touristy than other beaches in Sri Lanka. Great for couples! Hire a couple of sun beds with shade to keep you out of the tropical sun well worth it!
title: Nice beach...

body: This beach is a little slice of paradise. White sands and clear water in a small bay fringed with palm trees. I loved the fact it wasn't too big, it only had a few bars/ eating places and wasn't over crowed with tourists. Moreover, if you take a little walk past the hut there's another little bay called fishermans bay which is so picturesque. You can't swim in the sea as it's too rocky but it would be great for snorkelling and it's very quiet. Being very much into photography the appearance was very important and I was able to take some great photos on this beach as it was so pretty, so it gets the seal of approval from me for that reason alone. I loved it here xo
title: My favourite beach in Sri Lanka

body: This beach is very crowded and quite small. There are much better beaches all along the coast from Dikwella to Rekawa. Not sure what the hype is about.. it's packed with hotel tourists and I didn't like it.. lonely planet should definitely update their info..
title: There are much better beaches in Tangalle

body: the hidden beach (next bay, to the west side) is much nicer though you cannot swim there, but only switch the beaches for a swim!
title: super for wave jumping and swimming

body: We were lucky enough not to be housed in the main Tangalle beach resorts but rather in one of the quiet and cheap guesthouses of Unakuruwa bay, so Goyambokka beach felt (a bit more) crowded and expensive compared to the rest of our Sri Lankan trip. All the restaurants are extremely expensive (1200 rps for ROTI, about 50* the normal price), a good option was guesthouse Rocky point (up the stairs on the southwest creek), which has nice curries and juices on a lovely terrace for a break in the shade. They have sun beds on the beach as well.The beach itself is very beautiful and with beautiful big waves, (a few local residents have warned us off swimming) but Silent beach next door has all the views, a wider sand shore and none of the crowds (ask pathway to residents as it can be tricky to find on the beach side, given that a hotel has privetized some of the paths, or use the main road).
title: Nice beach but ...

body: this beach is very different from other beaches in Tangalle. It's a small golf and very private/ there are some resorts there looking fantastic
title: very special beach

body: the views are ok, but the beach is short, sunbeds are expensive, restaurants are poor. beware of "beach view restaurant" - worst food we have tried in sri lanka, moreover it was expensive
title: overrated

body: Some days there are huge waves, but they are so far out, that you can swim anyway, even with small children. The children thinks it´s great fun to play in the waves.The sun beds can be quite expensive (1000 rupees each) if you dont buy sea food.
title: Nice and fun beach, but expensive sun beds

body: This is one of the most beautiful beach we have yet to have seen in Sri Lanka .definetly worth a 2 day visit. If it is nothing you want to do this is the right place.all of the beach cafés have the same price except when you walk a little through the rocks( right side) you will come across with Think restaurant. Wonderful people and wonderful place.must visit.
title: Wonderful

body: This was the BEST seafood we ate in Sri Lanka! It may look unassuming but the food was seriously delicious. Possibly the best grilled prawns I've ever had and my boyfriend's devilled calamari was equally awesome. Just delicious. I want to eat here everyday, forever. Beach was sublime too.
title: Greetje Restaurant

body: Beautiful place, really impressive, a hidden gem! You can stay at Rocky Point, which is a simple but well located b&b.
title: Let's have dinner directly on the beach with candles

body: We ( family of 4 with 2 teens ) have just spent 3 days before moving onto Mirissa, this beach is beautiful with good waves and clean. There are 4 / 5 beach shacks here, we thought over priced for what they can serve. We were told no tea or coffee, no toilets and no where to wash your hands. I wonder what the chef does but no taking away from the fact the beach is beautiful, we were lucky our hotel 2 mins in tuk tuk away or a 10 mins walk to go toilet.
title: Beautiful Beach

body: Smallish beach, but beautiful and very relaxed. We spent four days here and it was perfect. Sea is not too rough to mess about in, but not suitable for swimming.Sri Lanka has a lot of dogs, and there are quite a few here. They don't bother you, but one lady near us was playing with one and was playfully bitten. I would definitely have rabies jabs if going back to Sri Lanka.
title: 4 days of bliss

body: We visited the beach during Ferbuary (in this time the sea should be calm). Beach is beatiful for watching and enjoying the wild nature. If you would like to enjoy swimmingin the sea, I can't recomend you. If you are not good experienced swimmer! Seriously be careful. I was swimming with my boyfriend in the waves and in the beginning it was ok. To swim over or under the waves seemed funny, but later really huge waves came and if I wouldn't be there with my boyfriend I wouldn't get out maybe. Sri Lanka has 3 drawn people per day, be careful guys 😃
title: Wild beach

body: Gorgeous beach.dont miss out Take a tuk and go just before sunrise. Don't forget to take a bottle of bear
title: Nearby

body: Amazing beach. Not too many people, and easy to get sunbeds. Small restaurants serves fish and simple but very tastefull meals. The water is not too deep which is good for kids, but waves was a bit rought sometimes.
title: Paradise

body: My version of paradise...water warm, waves big enough to play in but not as dangerous (according to locals who advised us) as other beaches in the area. The surf was too rough for our younger child but our son had a good time.
title: Beach for family in Tangalle

body: Clear water and clean sand. Beautiful scenery and a couple of beach bars made this a place to enjoy for a couple of hours while sipping a lime soda that only cost £1.It was fairly busy even though it was a quiet time of year. Most of the loungers and umbrellas were taken but we found shade from a tree.Definitely a beach to visit.
title: Safe for the belly board

body: The beach is perfect for swimming children to play in the waves and on the sand. There are a few beach bars to satisfy thirsty and hungry
title: paradise beach

body: It's a 10 - 15 minute auto ride from Tangalle. It cost us 200 LKR.It's 3 mins away from main road, so take the tuktuk drivers mobile and call him for a ride back.The beach has 4 shacks, beds, sheds. The shacks offer decent food and drinks.It's scenic, so do wander around the end of the beach. Sea is rough at times, but that is usual in Srilanka.Downside - does not have a public restroom, not even the shacks.Sometimes there are small sharp rocks in the beach. Small but possible chance of cuts and bruises. My friends toe end got cut.
title: Scenic beach but limited facilities

body: Wonderful beach with nice beach restaurants with fantastic sea food. The massage hut at the corner of the beach offered nice massage treatment in a wonderful frame of sound of the waves.
title: Best beach in Sri Lanka

body: Goyamboka beach is by far the most beautiful beach that we have seen in Sri Lanka! Unfortunately we just stopped there on our way from unawatuna to tissa but next time this is definitely the place we will choose for a beach stop!!
title: Most beautiful beach that we have seen in Sri Lanka!

body: this is one of the good choice of our selection. friendly and helpful staff. nice beach to relax with the kids. safe.
title: nice

body: Nice local beach. The waves here are pretty high but when you accompany your child the sea is much fun.
title: Oké beach

body: Beautiful beach, clear water and it's not crazy busy. There aren't a tonne of restaurants so the palm trees are still lining it. Gorgeous!
title: Favourite beach of our trip! (So far)

body: Sunbed 500rs!! Wtf. Lovely to swim and relax but bring your own blanket because those totally overpriced sunbeds.
title: Nice beach.

body: Very good beach, clear water, good (green) surfing waves. The restaurants are rather simple, not sure I would eat there. For surfing it can be a bit crowed so better to come early morning for that. You can rent surf boards at low rates.
title: Best beach in the area

body: Not very crowded but with the possibility to have some food and drinks. Clean, realaxing and quiet! 👍

body: Great surf, always a Tuk Tuk on hand to pick up or drop you there - quiet beach, family friendly with food and drinks available nearby
title: Quiet beach gem tucked awa

body: This is a very beautiful beach located near Tangalle.You could visit it with TukTuk or by foots.There are situated few restaraunts and some beds. For use of beds you should order some dinner at restaraunts.Another beautifully beach (Amanwella) situated not far from this place.

body: If you are not into the busy, touristy, music and bars of Mirissa and other places on the coast, this beach is an ideal little intimate beach with a gorgeous landscape.

body: Very crowded beach with tons of families. The rocks were cool and the palm trees provided the perfect amount of shade, but if you want something more privet - I recommend Medaketiya and Medilla for pristine empty beaches that stretch for miles.

body: We were told that the tangalle beaches are beaugtiful but that the sea was almost always to rough to swim. However Goyambokka beach proved this wasn't true. The beach is a positioned in a lovely cove sheltered by large rocky headlands either side. Although there were big waves, they broke further out and there was a wide calm shallow area that stretched a good 50 meters out to sea. This provided excellent paddling and warm swimming.

body: We have been in Sri Lanka for a week now and have been having had an exquisite time. Welcoming people, awe inspiring landscapes, clean and cosy lodgings.That was until last night. We hadn't realised the new year celebrations were going to last a week. So for the past few days we have had some issues with getting around (no buses) and with ordering food (limited options).No biggie.Last night we had planned to visit Break Point Restaurant but alas it was not operating. As we had had a fabulous lunch of grilled prawns and the best chips we've had in Sri Lanka by and large we decided to go back to the shack on the beach.The shack appears to be operating under the name Bamboo (that's what's written on the menus) and is the first one on Goyambokka beach if you're walking from rocky point beach. It's the last one if you're walking from Anantara, Palm Paradise or that direction.As my lunch there had been delicious (my friend's vegetable roti was sub par but we decided we'd stick to seafood) we went back for dinner. It hadn't opened yet and we saw one restaurant further down had opened so we decided to go there for an appetizer. We got grilled lobster with chips and a couple beers. Delicious. The guys there were adorable. We should have stayed there. But we wanted to have a different vantage point and shift places for fun.As we walked to Bamboo, which had lit lanterns, we noticed there was no one there. So we started walking back, when we were hailed by a dude saying he was the owner of Bamboo and we could have dinner. I sensed something was amiss but we decided to sit down anyway.When he came to take out order it was clear he was drunk and had been partying all day. That's fine but then why come open your shack? Just stay out partying. Our order appeared too confusing for him so we settled for ginger beers and a bottle of water. He asked repeatedly if he could sit down with us. Not being comfortable nor in the mood to be chatted up by a drunk stranger we politely but firmly refused. He would have none of it and sat down anyway, bringing with him a bottle of Arrack. He offered a drink of this and when I asked for the price he said it was "no charge". Obviously I wasn't going to accept free drinks so I offered 500 for a glass.Anyway the problem wasn't money. The problem was this dude's being upset by us refusing to chat with him. We decided to cut our stay short and go back to our hotel. The dude followed us on the beach and we found him quite menacing. In the end my friend gave him an extra 1000 rupees and he finally left us alone.
title: Awesome beach but scary dudes.

body: Save for children however not good for small children and great swimming some time there are rough waves

body: We were advised to stay here by a local resident as it is safe for swimming (one of the few 'safe' beaches in Tangalle). But be warned, the waves are quite big throughout the day, and somewhat intimidating for small children and inexperienced swimmers. The beach restaurants here are not good - slow service, poor quality and rip off prices. If you want calmer beaches for swimming, best to head west to Weligama.
title: One of the few safe beaches in Tangalle but not for for the faint hearted swimmer!

body: This is a beautiful beach with a calm sea for swimming. There are a few cafes with sunbeds and umbrellas - you just need buy a drink/snacks from them. It was peaceful and not too crowded, the only downside was there didn't seem to be any toilets but we only spent a couple of hours there so didn't matter to us.
title: Beautiful beach

body: Rough waves - not good for small children. We enjoyed walking next to the beach every day, watching the fishermen, the palmtrees, the wild ocean and big waves. But swimming in the ocean is not the best if you are travelling with small children. Even for adults, it can be a little trying with the big strong waves. My suggestion is to book a hotel with a swimming pool, such as the Villa Tangalle Lagoon, which is a great place next to the river and close to the beach as well.
title: Rough waves in the afternoon.

body: this is an amazing beach, lovely sand and fun waves to play in. Unfortunately the only time I've had a disagreement in our whole stay in Sri Lanka was here. When we arrived we were offered a deck chair in the shade if we bought lunch at the mans restaurant, or if we didn't buy we would pay a fee. We agreed, taking deck chairs under a dodgy umbrella that was more frame than coconut leaf but within half an hour this was under cover of a tree so this was fine. We bought a few drinks and had a nice morning, but when we were ready for lunch the restaurant tables were full. And on closer inspection all the tables seemed to be sharing one plate, and no one looked happy to be there. So we decided to go elsewhere. The owner then demanded 1500 rupees as we weren't buying lunch, which we had not agreed to but appreciate our fault in not agreeing a fee at the beginning. After an unpleasant chat, pointing out that we had bought drinks and he had no free tables, I gave him 300 rupees, which he ripped up. We walked off, he ran after us but luckily we were staying at a place very nearby.TLDR: Lovely beach, agree a fee and check the food/menu before using deck chairs. And avoid the middle restaurant as no one seemed happy to be there. (Hint to the owner, a good business has happy customers, not just ones that are forced to eat there)

body: The beach itself is very beautiful. The problem are the amenities. body: Nice small strip of beach almost a private beach sort of with 4 beach restaurants operated by locals around the area. Walking distance from hotel anantara and directly in front of palm paradise cabanas/villas. If you want to try surf boardschool it is a good place. Also try out beaches around Arugambay/pasikudha in eastern coast of Sri Lanka which are fantastic.
title: Goyambokka beach Tangalle

body: Located 100m south of Matara Road, it's very easy to reach with a pleasant walk (45 minutes) from Tangalle. A wonderful beach with clean yellow sand and turquoise water (be careful of high waves!). Umbrella and sea beds available on site: rental is free if you have lunch there (Phoenix restaurant is strongly recommended!)
title: An excellent and clean beach near Tangalle

body: Very beautiful small beach, but not much to do apart from sunbathing. Very big waves and strong currents. Beachrestaurants expensive and not very cosy.
title: Beautiful beach

body: My husband and I spent about four hours here and liked it. It's not a huge beach but good enough for a fun swim in the waves!We were told that we had to pay to rent the sun beds, or they would be free if we had something to eat. We came in around lunch time so we decided to have some seafood rice after our swim.The waves were a lot of fun and not as dangerous as a lot of other areas! We got to rent boogie boards (300 rupees an hour) and had an awesome time!
title: Fun afternoon boogie boarding!

body: The best beach in tangalle.Quiet beach with nice restaurants.Perfect for families and couples.The sea is really clean
title: Beautiful beach

body: beautiful beach with confortable sea beds, nice stuff, fresh sea food, delicious taste, but small serving for price, which is quite expensive.
title: Nice stuff, beautiful beach

body: We definitely made the right choice, this beach is lovely and the Peacock Garden Cabanas are a fabulous place to stay while you're there.Be sure to have dinner on the beach by candlelight!
title: Beautiful and remote feeling

body: Best beach in Tangalle by miles. Great for swimming and sunbathing and relaxed eating on the beach. Not good for snorkelling.
title: Best beach in Tangalle (that I know of!)

body: A paradise. A wonderful place to see if you like to enjoy a beach with palms, sand, sun and few people.
title: Tropical paradise

body: We spent a few days near hear and enjoyed this beach a lot, although it can get quite busy. The waves are great for playing in although might be a bit strong for small children. They also have boogie boards you can borrow at the cafes which were great fun.
title: Nice beach with fun waves!

body: We came here for a massage and wanted to spend the rest of this day at a beach. Too many touists at this beach, food was the worst I have eaten so far in Sri Lanka and it was a bit expensive, big waves. There are 4 small restaurants at this small beach. Maybe if there are less people, I would visit this beach again.
title: Average beach

body: Good for relaxing and for having fun with waves. There are few bars and restaurants. It is nice but it is definitely overrated, after half a day you will probably get bored.
title: Overrated but still worth a visit

body: When we arrived at the beach, they wanted 300 rupees for two sun beds, if we bought lunch. After a while they came with the menu and there was nothing that looked good, so we just wanted to pay for the sun beds. All off the sudden, the price had rise to 1500 rupees for the same two beds. We just left and will never come back to this hustler place. There is a lot nicer or similar beaches we would choose instead.
title: Too expensive

body: We loved the beach at Goyambokke. It's not to busy and the sea was nice and warm. There are several little restaurants serving sea food and we had lunch in the one on the middle of the beach.The owner/chef speaks excellent English and sends his guys out to get whatever you want ... Lobsters prawns etc.It was my wife's birthday so we arranged to come back in the evening and he organized lobsters a bottle of wine we requested and we had the most amazing supper on our own private beach with our own private chef .... Delicious and an awesome experience that is hard to find in this overcrowded world of ours. His place is the one under the big palm trees on the centre of the beach her has four tables in the front row of tables and some loungers in front and boogie boards for hire
title: Best beach in Tangalle

body: Small beach not far from main road, surrounded by chalets and resorts. Sandy, rocks at both ends. Beach umbrellas provide shade, 4 or 5 places to get lunch or drinks. We went on a windy day so big waves. Water not cold. Also went in high season and beach not crowded so we worth a visit
title: Totally amazing

body: Small beach but has got good waters if you want to jump at some waves. Avoid the food is possible. Expensive and awful food.
title: Good fun if you want to crash with some waves

body: The beach is only quite short, but there's also very few people, so it doesn't matter. There are 4 separate bars on the beach, each with a set of umbrellas for renting. They don't charge anything for renting if you buy from the bar. There's nothing better - just take one of the umbrellas, and drink young coconut water. They're all reasonably priced, drinks at 100-200 ruppies (100 for coconut) and food for 400-1000, 1000 being a fresh grilled fish.Nobody is pushy, there're few solicitors, but they just let you be if you only shake your head.The waves were high enough for having really good fun (for an inland guy who sees a sea once per year maximum :) ), yet not too high so you could not swim there.There are no surfers on this beach and you can borrow those short boards for swimming from one of the bars.Overall, we spent 3 days on this beach and it was a really nice experience.
title: Excellent little beach for both fun in the water and relaxation

body: It is a truly blissful beach with stunning sand and kept really clean. The under current is a big strong but the sea is so lovely and warm.
title: Amazing beach

body: Great beach for swimming and body surfing. beach is clean of rubbish and there are 2-3 discrete bars/cafes.Local tuk tuk drivers try and run a cartel to keep prices high for foreigners. Call Said for tuk tuk services at very reasonable/local rates Said mobile +94 77967 9204 local call 0779679204
title: Lovely beach with waves

body: Goyambokkah beach is a small secluded beach in Tangalla. Calm swimmable waters with some waves that will sometime carry you back to the beach (fun). One of the more charming aspects of the beach is that it is not crowded and just barely developed. The beach is unspoilt and the few shacks that serve food do it well to humane prices (try the grilled fish for an unexpected amazing taste experience). A great place to catch some sun and play in the water.
title: Picture perfect beach

body: This is a beautiful beach,but sadly you can only paddle as its not really suitable for swimming due to the currents and waves.But to sit in a bar or restaurant and take in the view is just the job.You cant have everything but the view is great.
title: Beautiful Beach

body: Bamboo is the most recent of the four snack shacks located on the beach. Please give my regards to Nuwan and Mahesh the owners/staff. The food was fresh and awesome. In addition to the lunch and drinks during the day they can provide a fantastic dinner as well if requested. All 4 of the Snack shacks on Goyambokka beach provide a great lunch and drinks.
title: "Bamboo" the new "snack shack" on the beach !

body: the beach looks nice but the same you could say about all tangalla and dickwella beaches. we were in November and it was impossible to swim due to huge waves. t
title: overrated

body: nice beach, we went there in the morning and it was empty! lovely and clean. there are sun umbrellas avalaible. on one side of the beach there's a huge resort with watchmen. it was not easy to find the access road
title: lovely beach

body: Great beach almost out of a tropical postcard. Couple nice restaurants but slightly busy beach compared to the nearby ones, worth the visit. Well recommended!
title: Paradise on earth

body: great beach but the surf was really strong, the beach is pretty small but very pretty, we ate at a week old place " bamboos" the food was excellent quality, worth a visit
title: stron surf

body: Goyambokka Beach is super beautiful and far away enough from the main tourism strip to be too crowded. And the best is the Eden Reverie Spa just at the beach! It is the best massage you can get in Sri Lanka and for such a reasonable price. Don't miss it!
title: Beautiful piece of earth and the best best massage there!

body: Nice beach near to Tangalle hidden in the palm trees. Beatiful view to the ocean, in sunny day without big waves water is crystal clean. There are many sunbeds at the beach, most of them hidden under umbrellas. You can use them if you will buy some drinks or lunch in local bars. When we visited this place there is no garbage on the beach. But still many dogs right there (they are not aggressive).
title: Lovely place

body: Probably the best place to choose for swimming in Tangalle.Not many people, good waves.There a few restaurants as well.
title: Best choice for swimming in Tangalle

body: A small beach with not many people, the sea is very clean and the waves sometimes high. It is possible to lie on the beds with umbrellas and they are for free in case you take a lunch in the local restaurant.
title: Nice beach

body: We went to a restaurant there (the one at the right end) and had fresh Lobster, which was really good!!!The small beach is very calm, not many people around, good for relaxing.
title: Lovely, lonely Beach

body: We were underwhelmed by tangalle in general but luckily we found this place which restored our faith. You can get a tuktuk for 200rps from tangalle. The beach is small, very beautiful and much nicer waves. Highly recommended.
title: Highlight of our time in tangalle

body: First place we have been to where they charge you for sun loungers... despite us buying plenty of drinks. The beach is mediocre, the reviews we have read do exaggerate a tad.We have found much more beautiful and serene beach during our time in Sri Lanka.
title: Overrated

body: We learnt of this little hidden beach after asking our tuk tuk driver to recommend a good beach and we were not dissapointed! As with most of Sri Lanka the walk to it was slightly littered but once you reach the beach it's a lovely cove, when we were there in October there was only one beach hut that served food and drink and they allow you to use the beds for free if you buy your lunch there which I recommend the White fish and salad... The best dish I ate in Sri Lanka!! The water is also perfect if you fancy some body boarding, the restaurant had 3 body boards that they let us use for free. The waves are best suited for fairly strong swimmers as the current can be quite strong. Definitely worth a visit :)
title: Great find!

body: i have been this place several time with my family . such a nice beach white sandy . November to aprill is best time for swimming. there is hotel called palm pardise cabana is near by to have you food requirement .
title: nice beach

body: Really surprised by others reviews! Although we visited I. Low season the beach was not up to the previous reviews. Very dirty with lots of washed up litter, no sun lounges or parasols like the photos suggest, very small cove with building work on huts etc on the beach. Sandbags piled up in many places. Lots of stray dogs. Other beaches are much nicer.
title: Disappointed

body: The beach is indeed beautiful. It is not big and not crowded. There are 3 small cafes..we were visiting the one on the very right (looking at the ocean) and the food was very good there (try calamari with salad). There is a very nice SPA on the very left of the beach (really recommend you!). However, there 2 bad points: the waves are too big to swim and there is no sun after lunch (it hides behind the trees).
title: Nice beach with little people, but impossible to swim

body: But you must go to the restaurant in the middle of the beach - cant vouch for the other two - ask for evening meal reservation - he doesnt have electricity so by candlelight only- magical location, lovely food, best caring service
title: best spot and best food

body: We spent 2 whole days just swimming and lying about on Goyambokka Beach. Beach beds, shade and food provided by commercial beach operators for a good price.
title: Great beach to hang out on

body: One of the most beautiful beach in Sri Lanka. I was there in March. There were a big waves without people. You can also find many kinds of bars and restaurants.
title: Nice beach !!!

body: pristine and clean beach situated in tangalle. quiet beach to your self with hardly any one pestering you and lovely waves.
title: beautiful beach

body: This beach has crystal clear bluish water and snowy bubbles appearing here like a velvet in blue cloth. This is near by tangalle town and covered with palm trees like small beach forest. This beach sorrund by small rockey hills and you will feel ultimate relaxation there. Good and safe beach even for small kids. They can do body surfing here. Mosticonic thing here is you can watch how sea eagles catch fish for their food. It is amazing. Small beach resturents and luxurious resorts are available here. Fresh sea food dishes are avilable in 10 $ onwards and rooms available 50 $ onwards.
title: crystal clear bluish goyambokka beach

body: Lovely beach for walking, with lots of fishing boats to look. Waves are medium, so it was nice to swim, I didn't feel threatend by them :) The whole atmosphere there was beautiful, with really beautiful deck-chairs and beach umbrellas.
title: Loved it!

body: amazing massage shack on beach with a lovely lady massurist who really knew her stuff- try it. Also 3 cafes which did amazing fish dishes. Go round the corner to the left and find a wonderful cafe on three levels-need to climb a ladder though.
title: beautiful beach

body: Our favourite beach in Tangalle. Nice to swim, beautiful warm, crystal clear blue water. A row of beach bungalows that will feed you and ensure that you are well hydrated. If you eat at a bungalow, you get to use their loungers and umbrellas for the day. Well worth it.
title: All you need from a beach

body: Great sandy beach and good for swimming if you like waves. Go to the middle beach bar which is on stilts. The others are terrible with uninterested staff.
title: Great swimming beach with waves

body: Small beach near Tangalle good for swimming.Medium sized waves .There are few restaurants and one spa in the area but i didnt tried their quality.
title: Nice small beach

body: Best restaurant and bar is Krishans its the one on stilts in the middle of the beach. Sun loungers are free if you have lunch (not just chips) try the prawns in garlic butter or the squid flash fried in garlic butter. If there's anything special you want just ask him he will get it for you.
title: Great beach for families excellent food

body: Think Place is a small family run restaurant with a man mad tree house / tower and a handful of tables but the best curried fried fish I've had in Sri Lanka. Its just to the right of the (main goyumboka beach opposite Palm Paradise cabanas. ) pass the three beach cafes on that beach and then you have to climb over some rocks on the right hand side of beach and you discover a smaller second beach were Think Place is hiding. Great food but maybe go round in the morning / day before and reserve a slot in the tree house for lunch - one dish only but what a dish and setting !!
title: Try THINK PLACE for food

body: It's a nice little beach with a few restaurants. At the time I was there it was safe to swim, no particular current.It's a clean, intimate beach, perfectly fine to spend a lazy afternoon
title: best beach in Tangalle for swimming

body: It was quite difficult for us to swim in the beach on Tangalle, so discovering Goyambokka Beach was a GEM! You can just visit any small drink and food shack on the beach and order a nice ginger beer and coconut before jumping into the calm AMAZING sea. This beach is amazing for swimming, body surfing and body boarding. A lot of tourists in the area, but everyone's relaxed and peaceful which is wonderful.
title: My favorite beach

body: This small beach is home to four beach cafés whose sunbeds take up practicallyy all of the available sand area above high tide. Great for those who love sunbeds but not so good for those who prefer a quiet beach. Bathing popular but watch out for the big waves. Accessed by bus (Rs10) or Tuk-Tuk (Rs200) from Tangalla. Look for fireflies and giant bats at night when the beach is quiet.
title: No space.

body: Lovely long beach for walking on with lots of fishing boats to look as as you wander along. Did not swim as it was a bit rough when we were there.
title: Best beach we saw to walk on.

body: Hi, to everyone who enjoy Goyambokka beach. Yes, this is a gem for most travelers to sri lanka. I really enjoyed this place. But,,,,,,, 10 years before, it was pure sandy beach that you could genuinely say private, but now it is full of beach restaurants or cafes and private beach beds. I advice every traveler who enjoy this beach and want to preserve it for the future, please please don't use those beach sacks. Every year it becomes more and more beach restaurants. As long as you are visiting them, there will be more next year. So. one day or sooner, you will not more enjoy the privacy of the beach, but busy dirty, crowded beach. Do you want that, are you really interested in preserving this beach for the future, please do not visit them, but ask for your guest house or hotel to prepare a packet of snack or juice for you. That will definitely help preserve this gem in future. Thank you.
title: The gem in danger

body: This beach is quite secluded but defo not undiscovered. Despite quite a lot of visitors it remains to be a tranquil place for relaxing and swimming. Nice massage place directly on the beach. Rs. 2.800 for 60 minutes full body.
title: Nice hideaway beach

body: It's a 4km walk or tuk tuk ride from Tangalle and worth it. A nice secluded beach with a few bars/eateries and great beach for swimming.
title: Fantastic beach!

body: Liked fact you can swim - nice places to eat - a bit touristy for me.Good choice of accommodation - we had good lunch here.Upmarket prices.
title: Picturesque but small bay where you can swim in Indian Ocean

body: Quite small beach with palms and a few beach restaurants. Defintely nicer than than Mirissa and a better place for swimming.
title: Great beach

body: lovely little bay with small restaurants with good fresh food. Good for any sort of wave riding and walks.
title: great body surfing!!!!

body: We stayed in Tangelle and just caught a tuk-tuk to Goyambokka Beach for 200LKR. It is just beautiful with the golden sand, palm trees and a really good swimming beach. There are a couple of places where you can grab a cool drink and something to eat. It is a small beach but still a bit undiscovered not like Unawatuna etc. you can easily spend a whole day just lying in the sun and swimming here.
title: Best beach in Sri Lanka

body: Small but very nice and swimmable beach with some few restaurants/bars run by some very friendly guys.
title: Tranquil during the day, get-togethers in the evening

body: Goyambokka is a lovely beach with 3 rustic beach bars serving food and drinks. They all offer free sun beds (although they expect you to buy something from the bar) they aren't pushy though and one day we just bought bottled water. The water is choppy but nowhere near as bad as we were expecting and you can still go for a swim. All in all a lovely beach however I worry when the complex next door to Palm Paradise is complete it may get ruined so go now whilst you can. There's only a handful of people on the beach at any one time so it's really nice and there's no 'lucky lucky' men either which was a relief. There is one guy walking up and down touting tours (don't buy from him, he's ridiculously overpriced).
title: Lovely beach, go before it gets spoilt

body: We pretty much had this gorgeous beach to ourselves. There's good surf (I don't think for actual surfing as the waves all run into each other randomly) and you walk over into the next little cove which is also paradise. There's a little place that serves juices too- Manith's makes a good papaya one.
title: Beach perfection

body: We found this beach after having lunch at Green Cabanas Hotel and couldn't recommend it more highly. There were big exciting waves and there was hardly anybody around.
title: Lovely beach

body: A small perfectly formed cove with 2 beach cafes, golden sand and very rough sea. The beach is very nice indeed, backed by palm trees and very little development.
title: "A little slice of paradise"

body: Sand not white, construction debris and junk at entrance not v appealing, waves come up high with only a small strip for sunbathing but water seems clean though shallow with a strong receding tow Did not use the beach shack so cannot comment.
title: Not a great beach

body: When we got there we tried to get down the rocks with the stroller and no one from the restaurant helped, while we were struggling down the rocks young lads who own the place were not doing anything just lounging about watching us! Also when we got down the rocks we wanted some sun beds and the note said if u had lunch here u get the beds free so we agreed with a person from the restaurant if we have some drinks here we get to have the beds, but when we were leaving and paying for the drinks another guy said u have to pay for the beds which were 1000 rupees for one bed! But then we spoke up and said hang on we agreed if we have the drinks we get the beds but then he said no and kept insisting us to pay so we left without paying!! :)
title: Terrible!!! :(

body: Beach is ok, although we didn't like the stray dogs roaming around, quite hard to get to but the worst beach shack ever is on the left hand side as you stand and look out to sea. The prices were expensive and we couldn't even get a decent sun bed....we were given 3 broken beds then had quite a heated debate over the ridiculous charge for a bed -it was agreed before hand then when we went to pay for our drinks the group of men running the shack tried to make us pay an extra 1000 rupees. The beach is fun and the waves are very strong-it actually snapped our daughters boogie board. Not a pleasant experience overall.
title: Not nice

body: A perfect little beach with a few restaurants that also have sunbeds and umbrellas. In July there are big waves but swimming was very good possible. At beach restarant Greetje you even have wifi!
title: Lovely little beach

body: First thing that struck me was the big waves, they are pretty high for new traveller to theese island oceans.Second thing that I noticed was the guy that owns the bar to the far left (from the beach). He really wanted to sell a lot of things all the time! Trying to be "friends", kind of annoying.. there were piles of plastic, and thrash on the edges of the beach. Sun is only shining during morning/midday. If you meet a guy namned Sri, let him be your guide. He was GREAT!
title: Funky but OK.

body: Lovely little bay of white sand, but the waves were VERY big and rough in July. You couldn't really swim in the sea. The cafés on the beach are quite poor, shabby and overpriced, also bad service and kept forgetting anything we ordered. Loungers are available free but only if you buy something from the cafés.
title: Go here when it's the right season

body: great white calm beach if you want to get away from the crowd, great small restaurants on the beach.
title: piece of heaven

body: It was calm, with not so high waves, ideal to rest and sunbath. There are two bars located on the beach, but the prices are quite high.
title: Small and peacefull

body: If you're after calm and naturally beautiful beach without tons of tourists spoiling it, it's a good choice. Waves quite big, still you can swim there.
title: Secluded and romantic place

body: I must admit the beach is really beatiful...we were 2 women travelling together and we both fell in love with it..small, still not crowded, peacefull for enjoying yoga, reading a book and having fun in the waves...but all this is overshadowed by harrowing experience and we just want to warn other girls...PLEASE, even the invitation to come for a coctail by the bonfire on the beach and to watch turtles ( from the owner and waitor of the restaurant on the left when facing sea) might sound great DO NOT ACCEPT IT AND STAY AWAY FROM THEIR DRINKS!!!! You might end up paying a lot for what otherwise could have been magical:(
title: Enjoy but be carefull!

body: Picturesque, uncrowded, paradise, just stunning. To eat go to the middle hut and ask for Christian the owner, the food is superb.
title: Wow

body: Best beach i have been too....very clean! Keep it like that please....i hope that people have respect for the not messing this paradise up!
title: Best and cleanest beach in sri lanka

body: Its a great place for everybody to enjoy..There are enough of fine rests and Hotels around with kind and hospitable crew.
title: One of the superb beach for relaxing in a cool and calm surrounding with warm Hospitality of Goyambokka rests.

body: A few years ago this was a stunning, idyllic beach, however unfortunately it has been spoilt now by lots of building, litter, loud music at the weekends and other negatives that tourism can sometimes bring if not managed correctly / responsibly.
title: Spoilt

body: This beach can get crowded in high season as it is too small for such a big cabanas complex nearby. Sunbeds are maintained by the staff of the beach restaurants and need an urgent uprade.
title: Nice beach but can be crowded

body: Beaches in Sri Lanka are often picture perfect with long stretches of pristine sand bordered by coconut trees under the tropical sun. However, the strong waves make swimming less than ideal. At Goyambokka, it is safer than elsewhere in Tangalle as it is a bay and does not have any undertow. However, the waves are very powerful, throwing swimmers in all directions, creating a potentially dangerous situation. Despite being a good swimmer, I was unlucky and caught by surprise by a wave and ended up injuring a rib as a was thrown against the ocean-floor. Have fun but be careful! In terms of getting there, a tuk tuk from town is 150 Rs if you negotiate a little, otherwise 200 Rs.
title: Idyllic beach with strong waves

body: Great little shack (centre of beach) for super seafood.Lovely waves - fun and not scaryNot too busy.
title: Lovely

body: Goyambokka is a true bounty beach with soft sand, palms and clear waters. The waves are quite powerful - you have to concentrate not to be knocked over. You can buy drinks and food at the three Beach bars, but it's expensive. You can easily take a tuctuc to Tangalle and back again (200 rupees each way), grab a lunch - and save money compared to eating on the beach.
title: Beautiful beach, heavy waves

body: There is no doubt that the location is is fabulous. However I would urge tourists to avoid Rock View on Goyombokka Beach and Emmalaya which Inder also owns. Inder has built his businesses on the back of theft, deception, bullying and intimidation of UK nationals and Sri Lankans. Behind the smiles you may see, are hidden fears and great losses. I've met him in both Sri Lanka and the UK, don't be fooled, stay well clear. Goyombokka is great, Inder is not, see what others have to say, have fun, enjoy the beach, sun and moonlight but don't get involved with this man under any circumstances.
title: Watch Out for Inder

body: I first fell in love with Sri Lanka in particular Goyambokka beach in 1999 having volunteered, worked and visited Sri Lanka many times and making friends. Unfortunately one of those friends was the 'owner' of the Rock View Restaurant Indi (Jayweera Patabendgie Pransana Indika Nilusia) also known as Ukku. Although appears charming and helpful as other reviews point out you need to careful. I experinced terrible behaviours from him and those who work there which have changed my life forever.. Yes Rockview has sunbeds, umbrellas etc. The food they serve is OK but overpriced.Goyambokka beach it is beautiful, I love and miss it. Please enjoy your holiday do not let it be ruined by using rockview, he does not discriminate, use the other restaurants and stay safe and be happy.
title: Take Care

body: This trip to Tangalle has left me scarred for life. The beach restaurant bar owner Indy drugged my drink, i blacked out and have no memory of what happened. The 4 star villa Maya Tangalle where i stayed recommended the bar, they even told me that the owner Indy is their friend. Can anyone tell me where i can seek justice for this?
title: Beware drugs in your drink

body: Arriving in Tangalle, I was eager for a swim. But due to the strong waves and warned by the locals, I couldn't. Apparently, October wasn't the best time to swim although it was OK to hang out on the beach. Luckily, I read about Marakolliya Beach further North so I had the best time there in the South. Surprised no one has written about that beach here.
title: Be Cautious!

body: Since the Tsunami carved out a lot of the beach sand, waves tended to dump closed to the shore. Once beyond the break, strong swimmers are fine. Not recommended for those unfamiliar with surf conditions.Great beach umbrellas provided by the Paradise Cabanas, and the beach cafe / restaurant provides great food and drinks. If you are looking for a place to relax by the beach, this is a good choice.
title: Need to be a good swimmer, best beach in Tangelle

body: The beach at Goyambokka is very small and when the tide comes in it`s mostly flooded.There a very ripping currents just a few meters offside the shore.
title: Very small beach.

body: Absolutely stunning beach but as the waves are very strong, I felt it unsuitable for children. There are bars on the beach but they are very expensive and the food isn't even that great.
title: Beautiful but a bit dangerous

body: Great beach to play in the waves, with 3 small small shacks to eat grilled fish and buy drinks. We were with kids (1 and 5) and it was a lot if fun. Our advice: avoid the shack at the left when facing the sea: the "Rock view". we found them,a bit tricky: they "didn't have change on 500 Rp" which we found hard to believe, the fish was not fresh and the guys were not very nice, especially the bald guy... Other than that: great beach !
title: Great beach to play in the waves, but avoid the "Rock View"

body: The beach is wonderful but we got some knockout pills in our drinks. The staff in the bars looked very reliable and they were very lovely. Even if we were 4 peeps (3 girls and 1 guy) we got some drops in our drinks. they wanted to show as the turtles but all 4 of us felt asleep while waiting. We were very happy that nothing else happened. Even if we called the police the next day, we are sure that the big guy without hair, who's name is "Indi", and who gave us the drops, is still there... Take care!
title: Attention: Knockout Pills
Be aware of being druged!
body: The Beach is nice enough, no doubt there! However, we witnessed how a girl passed out after eating at one of the places at the beach. They obviously thought she was alone, but her friend was just away for a couple of minutes. Hence, she luckyly only had to spend a night at the hospital and it turned out that she had been drugged.

title: Stunning
body: Simply beautiful. An amazing beach with waves to jump. Can't swim there but can cool off with the breakers. Around 3 small beach bars. Just a few other tourists. All wonderfully relaxing. Stayed in a small Guesthouse two minutes from the beach. A blissful two days.

title: Best beach in Tangalle
body: Beautiful little bay hidden down a small track next to Palm Paradise Cabanas- great for swimming even in the offseason, a few little drink shacks and sun loungers on the beach.

title: Idyllic setting
body: Everyone's dream of a tropical beach. Fabulous view to the ocean, clean beach and ocean, palm trees.

title: Perfect
body: Simply the best beach I have ever visited.Stayed locally in Goyambokka so the beach was 2 mins from our guesthouse.For the two days I spent here there was no more that 20 people on the beach. There's a basic selection of sun loungers to use and a wooden shack that sells drinks and serves simple seafood dishes.The main draw is the beautiful beach and water so clear it has to been seen to be believed.

title: Beautiful secluded beach, but be cautious of rumours we heard.....
body: Goyambokka is a small beautiful secluded beach location, and essentially serves approximately 3 hotels within the area so doesn't seem to get too crowded. It has great and safe swimming, and there are loungers etc to relax on. The sun tends to disappear around 4pm, so best to get out early in the day to make the most of the sunshine.A few hundred meters over some rocks is another beach area which is absolutely stunning, almost unused so great if you want some peace and quiet - there are no loungers but the calm and tranquility would make up for this.The beach has limited facilities, no toilets and 2-3 bar areas which serve drinks and a limited selection of food. One of the beach huts stays open during the evening for a bit of lively entertainment, although a word of caution we heard a fair number of rumours about European women having drinks spiked. We didn't visit or experience this directly, but heard a few conversations referencing this so ladies please be careful with what you order, don't accept free drinks and make sure you see it being made or order something that can be opened at your table. I'm sure it is all ok but better to be safe than sorry!!

title: The best beach in Sri Lanka
body: I have fought the idea of not reviewing Goyambokka Beach, for the fear of too many people going down there and ruining it. But then again, selflessness prevailed. So, I would like to say at the outset, please dont commercialize or ruin this beach! The beach is 5 min from the main Matara Road. We took two separate roads - one which has small guest houses/ villas on either side, and the other (which is shorter) is quite desolate. Goyambokka and Pallikaduwa are twin bay beaches. We spent our time at Goyambokka. The beach is large and clean. The water is shallow, but the waves over 8ft tall (in April). The water lovely shades of green and blue. It is in fact one of the coves in Tangalle. There is a wooden hut on the beach which serves up a few dishes and drinks. Apart from that, there are plenty of deck chairs to laze about on. That is pretty much it. Just a LOVELY LOVELY small beach.
